failures.title: Vauxhall B15DT Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing chain wear - all B15DT variants from 2018
items.whatHappens: The B15DT uses a timing chain rather than a belt, but the chain tensioner can wear on higher-mileage units, leading to chain stretch and eventual rattling on cold start. If ignored, the chain can skip teeth, causing valve-to-piston contact and a full write-off. This is a well-documented pattern across PSA DV5 family engines.
items.repairVsReplace: A timing chain kit replacement is viable if caught early (typically £800-£1,200 fitted). If the chain has skipped, the engine is frequently a write-off - replacement is the only economic route. → Read our full timing chain failure guide

items.title: DPF clogging - urban-use B15DTs
items.whatHappens: Like all modern diesels, the B15DT's DPF (diesel particulate filter) clogs with repeated short, cold urban journeys where regeneration cycles don't complete. Symptoms include reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and eventually a blocked DPF warning light.
items.repairVsReplace: A forced regeneration or DPF clean (£300-£600) can resolve early clogging. In severe cases, DPF replacement (£600-£1,200) is required. → Read our full DPF failure guide

failures.goodYearsLine: The B15DT was introduced in 2018 and has seen no major revision-level failures reported. Later Euro 6d-temp units (2020+) incorporate improved AdBlue systems that are less prone to NOx sensor failures than earlier Euro 6 units .

variants.title: B15DT Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: The B15DT is the Vauxhall/Opel designation for the PSA Group's 1.5-litre DV5 family diesel. The same physical engine appears under multiple sub-codes across the Stellantis group, with different power outputs and emissions calibrations for different vehicle applications . - Fitted to: Vauxhall Vivaro C, Combo D, Zafira Life - Key technical difference: Lower 102hp tune, Euro 6d compliance, calibrated for light commercial duty cycles - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family timing chain and DPF patterns above - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with higher-output variants; ECU and injector calibrations differ - fitting a 130hp unit to a 102hp vehicle without ECU reflash will cause running issues - Fitted to: Vauxhall Astra K, Corsa F, Crossland X, Grandland X, Mokka B - Key technical difference: 130hp high-output calibration, Euro 6d-temp, different injector mapping - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family timing chain and DPF patterns above - Interchange note: The D15DTH can replace D15DT in some applications with ECU recalibration, but always confirm loom and sensor compatibility - Fitted to: Vauxhall Astra K, Combo D, Vivaro C - 2020+ production - Key technical difference: Revised engine management calibration, AdBlue system updates - Sub-code-specific failure note: Reported fewer AdBlue-related NOx sensor failures than earlier DV5 units - Interchange note: Can swap with D15DTH in same chassis, but check DPF/AdBlue module compatibility - Fitted to: Vauxhall Vivaro C (Peugeot/Citroën van variants) - Key technical difference: Same 130hp output as D15DTH, different ECU calibration for van duty cycles - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family timing chain and DPF patterns above - Interchange note: Generally interchangeable with D15DTH; always verify with a Vauxhall specialist before ordering - Fitted to: Astra K, Corsa F, Crossland X, Grandland X, Mokka B - Key technical difference: Factory plant designations for the DV5RC (130hp) variant - no mechanical difference from D15DTH - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family timing chain and DPF patterns above

relatives.code: the B15DT replaced the older 1.6 CDTi across most Vauxhall models from 2018. The older 1.6 unit had a stronger reputation for reliability but suffered from more frequent DPF issues in urban use
relatives.description: the B15DT's AdBlue system was designed to reduce NOx without compromising regeneration cycles.

variants.closing: The engine code is stamped on the engine block, typically near the front or on the cylinder head - visible from above on most B15DT installations. The full engine code also appears on the V5C registration document and on the build sticker in the door jamb or under the bonnet. Enter your reg above and we'll confirm fitment before you quote.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement B15DT - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used B15DT can make sense for lower-value hosts like an older Corsa or Astra K where the vehicle value sits under £5,000 . However, insist on timing chain history and known mileage - a used B15DT with 80k+ miles is an unknown risk unless documented. Fine for low-value cars; high-risk for a primary vehicle. See our used engines guide.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper recon on a B15DT replaces the timing chain and tensioner, injector seals, DPF clean (or replacement), and a full gasket set - directly addressing Section 5's failures. For most B15DTs in a Grandland or Mokka valued at £6k-£14k, a reconditioned unit is the right call: predictable cost, 12-month warranty, no hidden history. See our reconditioned engines guide.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild only makes sense when the host vehicle is high-value (e.g., a late, low-mileage Grandland or a commercial Vivaro with business value) or the engine has a specific component failure (e.g., a single failed injector that didn't damage the block). An upgraded rebuild with new injectors and a revised timing chain tensioner (if available) offers the longest service life. See our rebuilt engines guide.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All reconditioned and rebuilt B15DT units come with a minimum 12-month warranty and can be fitted through our nationwide network of vetted Vauxhall specialists - supply-only or full supply-and-fit available. See our supply and fit service.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The B15DT sits in vehicles ranging from a £2,500 Corsa F to a £15,000+ Vivaro van . For a Corsa or Astra with market value under £4,000, a reconditioned B15DT at £1,300-£2,200 approaches 40-60% of the car's value - evaluate carefully against the rest of the car's condition. For a Grandland or a working Vivaro, the same recon cost is financially sound. Always check current market value before committing to a replacement.

mainEntity.name: Is the B15DT a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B15DT is generally reliable for a modern diesel, but the timing chain tensioner is a known wear point that needs attention at higher mileage. Avoid repeated short urban trips if possible - this engine needs regular motorway runs to clear the DPF. Later production units (2020+) appear to have fewer AdBlue/NOx sensor issues than earlier examples. Timing chain inspection at 80,000 miles is strongly recommended. Use the correct low-ash oil (Vauxhall Dexos-spec) for longevity. Most owners report 120,000+ miles with routine servicing.
